# lfreleng-actions egress allow-list.
#
# Consumed via harden-runner-block-action (see README.md), which
# strips '#' comments and collapses all whitespace -- including these
# newlines -- into the single space-separated string harden-runner's
# 'allowed-endpoints' input expects. Edit this file exactly as you
# would any other list: one host[:port] entry per line, sorted
# alphabetically (LC_ALL=C). Where the reason for an entry isn't
# obvious, add a '# comment' directly above it explaining why it's
# there.
#
# A '*.host' entry matches exactly ONE label. Verified by probe
# under 'egress-policy: block', because upstream documents neither
# case: '*.ubuntu.com' admitted 'archive.ubuntu.com' but blocked
# both 'azure.archive.ubuntu.com' and the bare apex 'ubuntu.com'.
# So any host two or more labels below the apex needs its own
# entry alongside the wildcard, and so does an apex host.
#
# Distribution package mirrors are a known gap. Fedora, EPEL,
# CentOS Stream, Rocky, AlmaLinux, openSUSE and Arch all ship
# default repository configuration that resolves a metalink or
# mirrorlist and then downloads from whichever third-party mirror
# it hands back -- hosts sharing no parent domain, varying by
# source IP and by the hour. The vendor wildcards below cover the
# metalink/mirrorlist endpoints and the vendor-owned content
# hosts, but nothing can cover the mirror network itself. Where a
# job needs one of those distributions, pin the repository
# 'baseurl' to the vendor-owned HTTPS URL below and clear
# 'metalink' / 'mirrorlist', rather than adding mirror hosts here.
# Each of these serves directly, with no redirect off-domain:
#
#   Fedora, EPEL  dl.fedoraproject.org
#   CentOS        mirror.stream.centos.org, vault.centos.org
#   Rocky         dl.rockylinux.org
#   AlmaLinux     repo.almalinux.org
#   openSUSE      cdn.opensuse.org
#   Arch          geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com
#
# Those vendor hosts are reachable over HTTPS, so no port 80 entry
# exists for them: the plain-HTTP URLs a mirrorlist hands back
# belong to third-party domains that no wildcard here can cover.
#
# Note that 'download.fedoraproject.org' is a redirector and
# 'dl.fedoraproject.org' is not; only the latter is safe to pin.
#
# The per-entry comments record provenance: the service, and the tool,
# action or task observed reaching it. Most were reconstructed from
# StepSecurity run data with the github-network-audit tool
# (https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/github-network-audit); a few
# entries (e.g. harden-runner's own control-plane) are not observed in
# that data and are annotated from first principles. Coverage is
# best-effort: correct or extend a comment whenever you touch an entry.

# AlmaLinux mirrorlist endpoint and vendor-owned content (repo,
# vault); both served over HTTPS. See the header note: this
# wildcard does not cover the third-party mirrors themselves.
*.almalinux.org:443

# Alpine Linux package CDN over apk (dl-cdn); container image
# builds. Wildcarded because apk's default repository host is a
# CDN under this domain rather than a third-party mirror network.
*.alpinelinux.org:443

# Arch Linux project hosts. pacman's default mirrorlist is a large
# set of unrelated third-party domains, so this covers only the
# project's own services; see 'geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com' below for
# the Arch-operated mirror worth pinning to.
*.archlinux.org:443

# CentOS Stream metalink endpoint and vendor-owned content
# (mirrors, stream, vault); all served over HTTPS. See the header
# note.
*.centos.org:443

# Debian package archives over apt (deb, security, ftp, snapshot);
# container/base-image builds. Wildcarded, and on both ports,
# because apt fails over between mirrors and Debian serves the
# archive over plain HTTP as well as HTTPS -- package signatures,
# not TLS, provide the integrity guarantee.
*.debian.org:443
*.debian.org:80

# Fedora and EPEL metalink endpoint (mirrors) plus the vendor's
# own master mirror (dl) and build artifacts (kojipkgs); all
# served over HTTPS. See the header note.
*.fedoraproject.org:443

# GitHub hosted-runner control plane (hosted-compute orchestrator and
# watchdog subdomains on GitHub-hosted runners).
*.githubapp.com:443

# GitHub user content (raw, release-assets, pkg-containers,
# github-cloud): raw file fetches, LFS objects, release assets and
# container layers.
*.githubusercontent.com:443

# openSUSE and SLES package hosts (download, cdn, provo-mirror).
# download.opensuse.org runs MirrorBrain and redirects to
# third-party mirrors, so pin to cdn.opensuse.org; see the header
# note.
*.opensuse.org:443

# Arch Linux project-operated package mirror (mirror, geo.mirror
# -- the latter also listed explicitly below, being nested).
*.pkgbuild.com:443

# Red Hat content delivery and subscription services (cdn,
# cdn-ubi, console). Unlike the community rebuilds, the Red Hat
# CDN serves content directly and never redirects off-domain, so
# this wildcard is sufficient on its own.
*.redhat.com:443

# Rocky Linux mirrorlist endpoint and vendor-owned content (dl,
# download, mirrors); all served over HTTPS. See the header note.
*.rockylinux.org:443

# Sigstore keyless signing/verification (fulcio, rekor, timestamp,
# tuf-repo-cdn): pypi-publish-action, python-build-action,
# zizmor-scan-action and ossf/scorecard-action.
*.sigstore.dev:443

# SonarQube Cloud API/scanner subdomains (api, scanner):
# sonarqube-cloud-scan-action.
*.sonarcloud.io:443

# SUSE subscription, update and registry services (scc, updates,
# registry); SLES container and package builds.
*.suse.com:443

# Ubuntu archives and runner-OS services over apt, dirmngr and
# update-motd: archive, security, ports, esm, changelogs, motd,
# snapshot and keyserver (the last also reached by the Sonar
# scanner via sonarqube-cloud-scan-action).
# Wildcarded on both ports because apt fails over between the
# mirrors in the runner's /etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt -- the Azure
# mirror over HTTP first, then archive.ubuntu.com and
# security.ubuntu.com over HTTPS. Pinning individual hosts breaks
# package installs (e.g. graphviz for docs jobs) whenever the
# primary mirror is unreachable.
*.ubuntu.com:443
*.ubuntu.com:80

# SonarQube analysis sensor cache (AWS S3); reached by the Sonar
# scanner via sonarqube-cloud-scan-action. Both endpoint forms are
# listed: the SDK addresses the bucket regionally
# (<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com) while the global form remains in
# use, and an allow-list entry matches the host it is given rather than
# the bucket behind it.
analysis-sensorcache-eu-central-1-prod.s3.amazonaws.com:443
analysis-sensorcache-eu-central-1-prod.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com:443

# default of setup-java (maven-build-action, gradle-build-action).
# The binary download 302-redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com.
api.adoptium.net:443

api.scorecard.dev:443

app-updates.agilebits.com:443

astral.sh:443

# Artifactory (ASWF); LF project artifact repository.
aswf.jfrog.io:443

# Ubuntu package archive over apt; the priority-1 mirror in the
# runner's /etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt (go-httpbin-action,
# python-build-action). Required in its own right: it sits two
# labels below the apex, which '*.ubuntu.com' does not match, so
# removing this line reintroduces the apt failover breakage.
azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80

# Yarn (classic) release downloads and the Yarn APT/RPM repo. Named

dl.yarnpkg.com:443

# cgit (AGL, FD.io): one Linux Foundation cgit instance answers for
# several projects under a single certificate, all four names below
# resolving to one address. tox reads pip constraints from it while
# building a docs environment, before pip runs, via
# -chttps://git.onap.org/doc/plain/etc/upper-constraints.onap.txt and
# its per-project equivalents. ONAP reaches it today through
# docs-workflows and tox-run-action; these sibling names are listed
# alongside because harden-runner matches on hostname rather than
# address, so one shared host answering to several names needs an
# entry per name, and a project adopting these workflows would
# otherwise fail exactly as ONAP did.
git.automotivelinux.org:443
git.fd.io:443

# LF RelEng: redirects to github.com/linuxfoundation. A block refuses
# the first hop before any 3xx returns, so the redirecting name needs
# an entry even though its target already appears below.
git.linuxfoundation.org:443
